findings.detected: secrets reads the secrets without naming one
findings.consequence: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository, including the secrets that no expression of the job names, and also every secret of the environment of the job when the job references an environment. The memory of the runner holds every secret that GitHub sends the job, and code that runs in a step of the job can read every secret in the memory of the runner. The harm comes from two kinds of code: an action that turns malicious, and code that an attacker writes and that a flaw of the job runs. The harm is each secret that one of the two kinds of code can read now and could not read if each job of each workflow that can read the secret named only the secrets that the job needs. findings.detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner (self-hosted) of a public repository
findings.consequence: anyone who opens a pull request can run their code on the runner, whose state persists for the jobs after it: their secrets, their tokens and the runner's network

findings.detected: secrets reads the secrets without naming one
findings.consequence: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository, including the secrets that no expression of the job names, and also every secret of the environment of the job when the job references an environment. The memory of the runner holds every secret that GitHub sends the job, and code that runs in a step of the job can read every secret in the memory of the runner. The harm comes from two kinds of code: an action that turns malicious, and code that an attacker writes and that a flaw of the job runs. The harm is each secret that one of the two kinds of code can read now and could not read if each job of each workflow that can read the secret named only the secrets that the job needs. In the workflows that name only the needed secrets, GitHub sends each job only the secrets that the job names, and code that runs in a job can still read every secret that the job names. An action counts in every job, of any workflow, that runs the action; the code of an attacker counts only in the jobs whose flaw runs the code of the attacker
findings.remedy: name each secret the job needs, secrets.NAME, and pick one by an if for each value of the matrix rather than by a secrets[...] whose name is computed

findings.detected: a value taken out of the secrets AZURE_CREDENTIALS is written where the runner prints it

When a container has such a value in its env, or in the username of its credentials, the runner prints the value unmasked in the docker commands that the runner prints at the start of the job, before any step runs. When no ${{ }} of the if calls a status function (always(), cancelled(), failure() or success()), GitHub adds success() && before the string, and the job or the step runs only when the jobs or the steps before the job or the step succeeded. When a ${{ }} calls a status function, even success(), GitHub adds nothing, the if is the string alone, and the job or the step runs after a failure too. When the if is written to keep an attacker from running the job or the step, the if does not stop the attacker: the rules of this linter that evaluate the if in the runs of an attacker read the if as true, as GitHub does, and read the job or the step as when the job or the step has no if: for example, dangerous-triggers reports a job that runs on an event of the attacker with secrets or a token that writes. What the attacker gets comes from what the job or the step does, not from the if alone
quality_findings.remedy: write the whole condition in one ${{ }}, such as ${{ a && b }}, or write the condition without ${{ }}, such as a && b; both forms work in a workflow and in an action.yml. In an action.yml, write nothing around the ${{ }}: no space, and no block scalar (if: |), which keeps a line break after the ${{ }}

quality_findings.detected: the env key DATABASE=URL has =, which no name of an environment variable can have, and the runner sets the variable DATABASE instead, to a value made from the rest of the key and the value written
quality_findings.consequence: no step gets a variable whose name is the key: the runner sets the variable named by the part of the key before its first = instead. For the key A=B with the value x, the value of A depends on where the key is written and where the step runs. For a key in the env of the workflow, a job or a step: a step on the runner gets A with the value B=x, and a step in the job's container gets A with the value B. For a key in container.env (the job's container) or in the env of a service container (services): the container gets A with the value B=x. For a key in runs.env of a Docker container action: the container of the action gets A with the value B
quality_findings.remedy: rename the key to a name without =, the name that the step reads

quality_findings.detected: the env key GITHUB_SHA names a variable that the runner writes in each step after the env of the step is set: the runner writes the value of ${{ github.sha }} over the value written
quality_findings.consequence: each step gets the value that the runner writes, not the value written in env; the log of the step shows the written value under env:, so the written value seems to reach the step. On a Windows runner, whose variables have no case, the same holds for the name in another case, such as github_sha; the rule reports such a name only in a job whose runs-on names a Windows runner
quality_findings.remedy: give the value a name that the runner does not write, and read that name in the step

quality_findings.detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command set-output, which GitHub deprecated
quality_findings.consequence: the runner adds a warning to each run of the workflow that runs the step. GitHub planned to disable both commands on 2023-05-31, and the notice of 2023-07-24 postponed the date without a new date. For set-output: once GitHub disables set-output, the step sets no output. For save-state: only the post step of the same action reads the state, and a run script has no post step, so no step reads the state that a run script saves
quality_findings.remedy: for set-output, write name=value to the file $GITHUB_OUTPUT; for a value of many lines, write the line name<<DELIM, the lines of the value and the line DELIM, where DELIM is a random text that the value does not contain. For save-state, remove the command, because no step reads the state that a run script saves

quality_findings.detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command add-path, which GitHub disabled
quality_findings.consequence: when ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is not true for the step, the runner fails the step. When ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true, the command works, and each line that the step prints as a set-env or add-path command sets the environment variables or the PATH of the later steps; a value of an attacker that such a step prints is reported by the rule unsecure-commands

quality_findings.remedy: use a version of the action whose runs.using is node24, ask the maintainer of the action for such a version, or replace the action with one that is maintained
